evidence.finding: Service level fell below the 80% target at 10:15 (75.0%) and 10:45 (77.42%).
ASA rose to 48.73 seconds at 10:15 and 47.73 seconds at 10:45, coinciding with the two service-level breaches.
At 10:15, 97 calls were offered versus 79 forecast (+22.8%); at 10:45, 93 were offered versus 76 forecast (+22.4%).
The two highest relevant demand peaks aligned exactly with the below-target intervals, and service recovered when offered volume declined.
All 49 scheduled agents remained logged in throughout the window, with 45 productive agents at 10:15 and 46 at 10:45; forecast requirements were only 39 and 38 respectively.
Pressure was localized by interval: General Service received 50 calls and fell to 63.27% at 10:15, while Account Support and Escalations fell to 70.0% and 63.64% at 10:45.
The breach was intermittent rather than sustained: service level recovered to 84.52% at 10:30 and exceeded 91% from 11:00 through 11:15.
No routing, platform, or other operational event was recorded.

primary_root_cause_detail: Short, interval-level demand spikes exceeded planned capacity and directly coincided with the service-level breaches. Offered calls reached 97 versus 79 forecast at 10:15 and 93 versus 76 forecast at 10:45, while staffing, AHT, and transfer rates remained broadly stable.
recommended_actions: Add intraday volume alerts when offered demand exceeds forecast by approximately 15% or more.
Maintain a rapid-response staffing plan for short peaks, including movable cross-skilled agents or deferred offline activity.
Review queue-level skill allocation so capacity can be shifted toward the queues receiving disproportionate interval demand.
Recalibrate short-interval forecast variability and staffing buffers around the 10:00–11:00 period.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained fixed at 49, productive staffing stayed between 44 and 46, and available staffing exceeded forecast requirements.
Adherence remained near its normal 90–94% range and was 91.84% and 93.88% during the breach intervals.
AHT during the breaches was 373.12 and 381.09 seconds, close to forecast and surrounding-period levels, with no sustained increase.
No routing-change event was supplied, and the queue-level pattern does not establish a configuration change or misrouting.
Queue divergence reflects where the demand peaks landed, but fixed queue staffing and localized pressure do not independently establish queue imbalance as the initiating cause.
There was no platform event or broad call-processing disruption, and performance recovered without a documented technical intervention.
Reported service levels reconcile to the supplied formula; for example, 72 divided by 96 eligible calls at 10:15 equals 75.0%.
No agents were in training during any interval.

stakeholder_summary: CC-014 was caused by two brief demand spikes that exceeded planned interval capacity, not by staffing loss, AHT inflation, routing change, or a platform issue. Calls ran about 22–23% above forecast during both below-target intervals, driving ASA higher and service level to 75.0% and 77.42%. Performance recovered as demand normalized, so the impact was intermittent rather than sustained.
